How to Measure Bra Size at Home: The Complete Step-by-Step Guide

Master the accurate 6-point measurement technique at home with a soft tape measure. Eliminate band riding, strap digging, and cup gapping forever.

Why Traditional Measuring Methods Fail

Most department stores and mall bra chains continue to use the archaic "+4 method"—adding four inches to your measured underbust before calculating cup letters. This formula was invented in the 1930s when bra fabrics were rigid cottons with zero spandex or elastane. In modern bras with elasticized wings, adding four inches places you in a band that is far too loose to carry weight, shifting 90% of the burden onto your delicate shoulder straps.

What You Need Before Starting

  • Soft measuring tape: Flexible sewing tape measured in inches or centimeters.
  • Mirror: To verify that the tape remains completely horizontal and level across your back.
  • Comfortable posture: Stand upright with relaxed shoulders. Do not suck in your stomach or puff out your chest.

The 6 Precision Measurements

Step 1: Loose Underbust

Place the tape directly beneath your breasts where the underwire sits (the inframammary fold). Keep the tape level across your back and pull it comfortably, as if wearing a gentle, relaxed garment.

Step 2: Snug Underbust

At the exact same position, pull the tape with moderate tension—the exact firmness you would want your bra band to hug you on its loosest clasp hook.

Step 3: Tight Underbust

Exhale completely and pull the tape as tight as you possibly can ("break the tape" tension). This identifies how much soft tissue compresses on your ribcage and prevents bands from shifting around during physical activity.

Step 4: Standing Bust

Stand tall and wrap the tape around the fullest part of your breasts, keeping the tape level. Ensure the tape touches the skin without denting or squishing breast tissue.

Step 5: Leaning Bust (90 Degrees)

Bend forward at the waist so your torso is parallel to the floor. Let your breast tissue hang freely with gravity. Wrap the tape around the fullest part. This crucial step captures true projection, especially for softer or post-nursing breast tissue.

Step 6: Lying Bust

Lie flat on your back on a firm bed. Measure across the fullest part of your chest. This captures your natural breast width and root footprint.

Frequently Asked Questions

Clear, anatomically sound answers vetted by professional bra fitters.

What kind of tape measure should I use? ▾

Use a flexible, soft fiberglass or sewing tape measure. Do NOT use a rigid metal carpenter's tape measure as it cannot conform to curved body contours.

Should I wear an unpadded bra or go braless when measuring? ▾

Measure without a bra, or in an unlined, non-padded, non-compressing bralette. Padded or push-up bras distort measurements and will lead to an inaccurate cup calculation.

Why take leaning and lying bust measurements? ▾

Standing alone often underestimates projected or softer breast tissue due to gravity. Leaning forward 90 degrees captures full tissue volume and root projection, while lying down measures how tissue settles naturally.

Sources & Standards
